key_insight: TEDDY is a small pediatric foundation model that learns from ICD-coded diagnosis histories to forecast future disease risk and visit timing.
clinical_relevance: It could help flag children at higher risk for many conditions, including rare diseases, well before a first diagnosis appears in the record.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Predicted future diagnoses using only prior visit information, with first-occurrence tasks compared against sex- and age-matched controls.
Evaluated across 797 onset-prediction tasks and also tested visit-timing forecasting.
evidence_signal: Across 797 disease-onset tasks, TEDDY achieved a median AUC of 72.0% and outperformed DenseNet, CNN, RNN, and LSTM baselines on 96-99% of tasks.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but the model was trained and tested at a single pediatric institution, and visit-timing calibration was imperfect in the median and long tail.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
